method.name: async_preload
method.description:
Declares a resource to load during startup. Like [method preload], [param path] must be a constant [String], and the result can be used in a typed constant. This is a keyword and cannot be used as a [Callable]. [b]Normal GDScript, including the editor:[/b] Behaves exactly like [method preload]. The resource is loaded synchronously when the script is parsed, with the same type checking and load errors. No background request is created. Parsing a script can happen after the game has started; this mode does not provide a project-wide startup barrier. [b]GD2CPP (native C++ export):[/b] The exporter collects resource declarations across the exported scripts. After engine services are initialized, all synchronous [method preload] resources finish loading before game autoloads and the main scene are initialized. WGodot then dispatches the [method async_preload] resources through [method ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request] and allows the game to start while loading continues. Loading may execute custom resource constructors or setters. On builds without thread support, loading runs synchronously. Generated accesses read the retained resource through a readiness check. Access before completion, or after failure, reports an error and returns [code]null[/code]; it does not wait or supply a placeholder. Poll [method WGodotPreloads.is_finished] and check [method WGodotPreloads.has_failed] before using these resources. The engine collects completed requests on the main thread each frame; reading status does not block until loading finishes. Constant arrays and dictionaries are materialized as a whole on first access. All resources in a container must be ready before its cached storage is created. An early access reports an error and returns an empty container without caching it. Keep synchronous loading-screen assets in a separate constant container from asynchronous assets. In GD2CPP, successful synchronous and asynchronous preloads retain strong references until application shutdown. Repeated declarations of the same resource path share one entry; if any declaration uses [method preload], it is loaded synchronously. Later [method load] or threaded loads using [constant ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_REUSE] reuse the cached resource. Explicit cache-ignore or cache-replace modes have different behavior. Use preloads for frequently needed resources whose memory should remain resident. A synchronous preload failure stops native game startup and displays an engine-owned error prompt. An asynchronous failure allows game logic to continue and is reported by [method WGodotPreloads.get_failures], so the loading screen can handle it. Resource-load completion does not guarantee that all GPU shader or rendering pipeline compilation has finished. [codeblock] const IMPACT_SHADER: Shader = async_preload("res://shaders/impact.gdshader")
func startup_ready(api_ready: bool) -> bool: return api_ready and WGodotPreloads.is_finished() and not WGodotPreloads.has_failed() [/codeblock] Use [method WGodotPreloads.get_failures] to display loading errors separately from the readiness condition above. Assets needed to draw that loading screen should use [method preload]. [b]Note:[/b] In GD2CPP, script preloads resolve to generated classes, not asynchronous resource entries. Use this keyword for resource assets; it does not defer native class registration.

annotation.name: @no_mangle
@no_string_mangle
@override
annotation.description: Marks the following instance method as intentionally overriding a method inherited from a base class. When [code]wgodot/gdscript/strict_override_checking[/code] is enabled, overriding an inherited method requires [annotation @override]. Marking a method that does not override any inherited method is an error. [codeblock] @override func _ready() -> void: pass [/codeblock]

annotation.name: @partial
@private
@protected
@readonly
@static_class
annotation.description:
Marks the following class as a static utility class. Static classes cannot be constructed or used as type hints. They cannot use inheritance or interfaces, and their members must be static or constant. [codeblock] @static_class class MathHelpers: const SCALE = 100
static func percent(value: float) -> float: return value * SCALE [/codeblock]
